guide.cobblegenetics.affinity.body: A hidden elemental leaning, usually one of its own types, with a strength grade. When it matches one of the Pokémon's own types it resonates: it gains extra EXP, up to +15% at strength S. In breeding, opposed affinities (Fire and Water, Dark and Psychic...) make unstable babies, while two different, compatible affinities give hybrid vigour (extra potential). Strong affinities make both effects bigger, and the stronger parent's affinity is the likelier to be passed on. Some mutations, like Elemental Drift, turn the Tera Type into the affinity.
guide.cobblegenetics.affinity.title: Elemental Affinity
guide.cobblegenetics.daycare.body: An unemployed villager near a Genetic Incubator becomes a Day Care Aide. Leave an Egg in the Incubator and the aide hatches it over time, sending the baby to your party or PC. While an aide is at work, "♥ Day Care" and the progress float over the Incubator, the Egg wobbles more as hatching nears, and clicking the Incubator shows the time left (sneak-click to take the Egg). Aides also trade berries and purification supplies.
guide.cobblegenetics.daycare.title: Day Care
guide.cobblegenetics.mutations.body: Mutations change looks, stats (through IVs), abilities or Tera Types. They appear on wild spawns, in breeding, on evolution, in harsh places, in thunderstorms and with Mutagens. Many are inherited, and some stay latent, waiting for two carriers to meet. Rare ones need others first.
guide.cobblegenetics.mutations.title: Mutations
guide.cobblegenetics.potential.body: The most important gene. A wild or hatched Pokémon starts with every IV at least at a minimum set by its potential (up to 12 at potential 100). Potential also counts while you train: at each level up its lowest IV can rise, up to a ceiling set by potential (31 at potential 100). Babies get roughly their parents' average, so high-potential parents make high-potential lines.
guide.cobblegenetics.potential.title: Genetic Potential
guide.cobblegenetics.prediction.body: Analyse two Pokémon one after the other: the second report shows the range of potential and stability their babies would have, the odds of each trait and which mutations could appear.
guide.cobblegenetics.prediction.title: Predictions
guide.cobblegenetics.shadow.body: Corrupted Pokémon drain their own stability and cannot breed or evolve until purified. Purification is slow but rewarding: purified Pokémon gain stability and friendship, and can receive mutations nothing else gives.
guide.cobblegenetics.shadow.title: Shadow Pokémon
guide.cobblegenetics.stability.body: How safely its genes copy. Low stability means more mutations, a bigger share of them harmful and wilder results. Shadow corruption drains it, and part of the damage is inherited. Gene Stabilizers repair it.
guide.cobblegenetics.stability.title: Genetic Stability
guide.cobblegenetics.susceptibility.body: Susceptibility is how often mutation chances succeed for this Pokémon, from half as often to one and a half times as often. Want mutations? Breed for it. Want a clean line? Breed it out. The size gene makes Pokémon larger or smaller.
guide.cobblegenetics.traits.body: Six Mendelian genes, one allele from each parent. Dominant alleles show with one copy, recessive ones only with two, so two carriers can surprise you with a rare trait like Shadowproof. From research level 4 the Analyzer shows the genotypes and predicts the odds for a pair.
guide.cobblegenetics.traits.title: Inherited Traits
guide.cobblegenetics.why.body: Every Pokémon carries its own genes, and they pass to its babies. Better parents make babies with higher IVs (stronger stats in every battle), fewer harmful mutations and a better chance of rare traits. The Breeding value at the top sums a Pokémon up, and the Analyzer remembers the best of each species you have analysed. Breed to beat it.
guide.cobblegenetics.why.title: Why breed?
